title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
text: Artificial intelligence is the field of computer science concerned with creating systems capable of performing tasks that normally require human intelligence, such as reasoning, learning, perception, and language understanding.

title: Machine Learning
text: Machine learning is a subfield of artificial intelligence in which algorithms learn patterns from data and use those patterns to make predictions or decisions without being explicitly programmed for every individual task.

title: Natural Language Processing
text: Natural language processing focuses on enabling computers to process, understand, and generate human language. Modern NLP systems commonly use neural networks and transformer-based architectures.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, commonly known as RAG, combines information retrieval with language generation. A retrieval system finds relevant documents or passages, which are then provided to a language model as context for generating an answer.

title: Vector Embeddings
text: Vector embeddings represent text as numerical vectors in a high-dimensional space. Semantically similar pieces of text tend to have similar vector representations, allowing systems to perform semantic search.

title: Information Retrieval
text: Information retrieval is the process of finding relevant information from a collection of documents in response to a user's query. Retrieval systems can use lexical matching, semantic similarity, or combinations of both approaches.

title: Transformers
text: Transformers are neural network architectures designed to process sequences using attention mechanisms. They became foundational to modern language models because they can model relationships between tokens efficiently.

title: Large Language Models
text: Large language models are neural networks trained on large collections of text. They can perform tasks such as text generation, summarization, question answering, and translation.
